bib.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Lille, France, 2015 (arXiv v8)

question: Can a generative model be both flexible and tractable by learning the reversal of a slow forward diffusion that destroys data structure?
hypothesis: Estimating small perturbations to a diffusion process is more tractable than describing the full distribution with a single non-normalizable potential, and a diffusion process exists for any smooth target distribution.
contributions: Diffusion probabilistic models: extreme flexibility, exact sampling, easy multiplication with other distributions (posteriors), cheap log likelihood evaluation
Training of models with thousands of layers/time steps
Upper and lower bounds on entropy production per step

method.summary: A fixed Markov forward chain gradually turns data into an identity-covariance Gaussian (or independent binomial). A reverse chain with learned mean/covariance (or bit-flip probability) per step, parameterised by MLPs or multi-scale conv nets, is trained by maximising a variational lower bound K on log likelihood. Sampling runs the reverse chain from noise; inpainting/denoising multiplies a function r(x) into each step.
method.task: density estimation / generative modelling, sampling, inpainting and denoising

datasets.name: Binary heartbeat
datasets.size: sequences of length 20, a 1 every 5th bin

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.split: training images fit; holdout used for K
datasets.preprocessing: uniform noise added to remove 8-bit quantization (per Theis et al. 2015); scaled to variance 1

datasets.name: Dead leaves
datasets.split: identical train/test as Theis et al. 2012

models.name: Swiss roll model
models.architecture: normalized RBF network, 1 hidden layer of 16 units; readout layer per time step, other weights shared across steps and both functions; fSigma diagonal, sigmoid-bounded

models.name: Binary heartbeat model
models.architecture: MLP with sigmoid nonlinearities, 20 input units, three hidden layers of 50 units; readout per time step, rest shared

models.name: Image models (CIFAR-10, MNIST, dead leaves, bark)
models.architecture: multi-scale convolution layers (mean-pool to powers-of-two scales, conv per scale, upsample and sum, softplus), then 1x1 conv dense layers (tanh), linear readout of 2J coefficients per pixel, time-dependent Gaussian bump readout; diagonal Sigma. CIFAR-10 adds a parallel dense pathway; MNIST uses dense pathway only

training.objective: maximise lower bound K on log likelihood (Eq 13-15); KL between forward posterior q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) and learned reverse step plus entropy terms
training.optimizer: SFO (Sum-of-Functions Optimizer) for all but CIFAR-10; RMSprop for CIFAR-10
training.regularisation: first-step variance beta_1 fixed to a small constant to prevent overfitting

other.beta schedule: Gaussian: beta_2..T learned by gradient ascent on K with frozen noise (footnote: fixed schedule as for binomial is just as effective); binomial: beta_t = (T-t+1)^-1
other.reverse final step: p(x0|x1) set equal to forward step to remove edge effect

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling of the reverse chain from pi(x_T)

parameters.inpainting: r(x0) set to delta function for known data, constant for missing; bark central 100x100 region replaced by Gaussian noise
parameters.denoising: CIFAR-10 holdout corrupted with Gaussian noise variance 1 (SNR = 1)

metrics.name: K lower bound on log likelihood
metrics.definition: Eq 12/14 on holdout set; variance-1 scaled data except binary heartbeat

metrics.name: MNIST Parzen-window log likelihood
metrics.definition: Parzen-window estimate from model samples using Goodfellow et al. 2014 code

baselines: MCGSM (Theis et al. 2012) on dead leaves
Stacked CAE, DBN, Deep GSN, Adversarial net on MNIST
isotropic Gaussian / independent binomial null model
eval.protocol: Single reported value per dataset; +/- given for CIFAR-10 and MNIST, without stated definition of the interval.

evidence.where: Sec 3 (continues: open source implementation of the algorithm, and RMSprop for optimization)

evidence.quote: These were the result of the model learning the 8-bit quantization of pixel values in the CIFAR-10

results.claim: Diffusion model beats the previous state of the art (MCGSM) on dead leaves log likelihood.
results.setup: Dead leaves, train/test identical to Theis et al. 2012; baseline MCGSM
results.table: Table 2, rows Dead Leaves MCGSM 1.244 bits/pixel, Diffusion 1.489 bits/pixel
results.note: Table 1 K for dead leaves is also 1.489 bits/pixel (a lower bound).

results.claim: On MNIST the diffusion model scores 317 bits by Parzen-window estimate, between Deep GSN and the adversarial net.
results.setup: MNIST, Parzen-window code of Goodfellow et al. 2014 on model samples; not the lower bound K
results.table: Table 2, MNIST rows Deep GSN 309 +/- 1.6, Diffusion 317 +/- 2.7, Adversarial net 325 +/- 2.9, Perfect model 349 +/- 3.3

results.claim: CIFAR-10 lower bound K on holdout data.
results.setup: CIFAR-10 with uniform dequantization noise, data scaled to variance 1; improvement over isotropic Gaussian 11.5 ± 0.2 bits/pixel
results.note: An earlier arXiv version reported higher bounds caused by learning 8-bit quantization (footnote 3).

results.claim: Heartbeat binary sequence learning nearly perfect: K -2.414 bits/seq vs true -2.322.
results.setup: binary sequences length 20, 2000 binomial diffusion steps
results.note: K from Table 1 row Binary Heartbeat

results.claim: Other Table 1 bounds: swiss roll 2.35 bits, bark -0.55 bits/pixel, dead leaves 1.489 bits/pixel.
results.setup: bark texture, holdout, data scaled to variance 1, T=500

results.claim: Reverse chains use T=1000 steps for images (500 for bark), 40 for swiss roll and 2000 for binary data.
Posterior sampling lets the model inpaint a large missing region in a bark image with long-range structure.
results.setup: bark texture model, central 100x100 pixel region replaced with noise

results.claim: The earlier version's higher CIFAR-10 bounds were an artefact of learning 8-bit quantization.

limits: No sample-quality metrics; only log-likelihood bounds and qualitative samples.
MNIST comparison uses Parzen-window estimates, which the authors note differ from their own consistent lower bound.
Training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, steps, layer widths, compute, seeds) are not stated; the text refers to the released code.
Footnote 2 says recent experiments suggest a fixed beta schedule is as effective as learning it.

terms.definition: Generative model defined as the endpoint of a Markov chain that reverses a gradual forward diffusion converting data to a simple known distribution.

figures.caption: Proposed framework trained on 2-d swiss roll: forward trajectory, learned reverse trajectory, drift term.
figures.why: Shows the forward-destroy and reverse-restore idea at a glance.

figures.caption: Log likelihood comparisons to other algorithms.

code.snippet: q(x(t)|x(t-1)) = N(x(t); x(t-1) sqrt(1-beta_t), I beta_t)
